met_analysis:
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 69°E to the north of Lat. 32°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over South Haryana & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood extending upto 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from above cyclonic circulation over Southeast Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood to North Bay of Bengal across Jharkhand, south Gangetic West Bengal & adjoining north Odisha extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough now runs from north Sub-Himalayan West Bengalto south Madhya Maharashtra across Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Vidarbha & Marathwada at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over North Gangetic West Bengal & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south coastal Odisha & adjoining Northwest bay of Bengal now lies over central Coastal Andhra Pradesh & adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian Sea off south Kerala coast at 5.8 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from Gulf of Mannar to Madhya Maharashtra across Tamil Nadu, Interior Karnataka at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Tamil Nadu at 5.8 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
